ana.ignoring_wind_cost:
Two different questions are tangled in "the cost of ignoring wind". I separated them, because they give opposite-looking answers and the advisor will ask about both.

A. THE COST OF THE AIR — HV4W05 vs HV4W00, bit-identical mission files, only `SIM_WIND` differs. This is the clean A/B.
- Flown makespan 1234.78 s vs 1207.88 s → +26.90 s (+2.23 %). On the disarm definition, +27.17 s. (The runner reported +27.00 s; the small difference is the per-aircraft GPS clock, see below.)
- The wind-ignorant plan's own prediction error grows from +0.20 % in the still air it assumes to +2.43 % in air it did not model.
- Per aircraft, the growth is far worse than the fleet figure suggests: B2 −0.01 % → +7.08 %, B3 −0.02 % → +6.22 %, A1 +0.20 % → +2.43 %. The HEROs, which fly the short strips, are hurt most.
- Flown fleet distance +0.532 km (31.137 → 31.670 km); distance prediction error 2.30 % → 4.05 %.
- Coverage 100.0000 % → 99.9586 %.
- Minimum separation 100.435 → 100.291 m, i.e. the wind eats 0.14 m of a 0.44 m margin.

B. THE COST OF IGNORING THE WIND MODEL — HV4W05 vs HV4W55, both flown in the same 5 m/s @270 air.
- Planned makespan 1205.51 vs 1260.45 s; flown 1234.78 vs 1281.91 s. THE WIND-IGNORANT PLAN FINISHES 47.13 s (3.68 %) EARLIER. Wind-aware planning does not make the fleet faster here.
- What it buys is prediction fidelity: fleet error 2.43 % → 1.70 %; per aircraft A1 2.43 → 1.70 %, B2 7.08 → 4.90 %, B3 6.22 → 2.88 %.
- DECOMPOSITION (this is the part that was missing): of the 47.13 s by which the wind-aware fleet finishes later, 44.0 s is a later SCHEDULED release of A1 (656.0 s vs 612.0 s in the plan) and only 3.23 s is a longer flight (A1 airborne 623.40 s vs 620.17 s). The wind model changes the schedule far more than it changes the flying.
- Flown fleet distance 31.670 vs 31.888 km, i.e. the wind-aware route is 0.219 km longer.

WHY THE REALIZED GAIN IS ZERO, AND THE LIMIT ON GENERALIZING: the survey strips run east-west and the wind is east-west, so the along-track component cancels between out-and-back legs — the same cancellation the project has recorded before. Residual risk #11 (strip azimuth does not rotate with wind) is the mechanism. This result must be stated as "for a wind parallel to the strips"; it says nothing about a crosswind case, and D1 has removed the 180° cell that would have tested it.

HONEST SUMMARY SENTENCE FOR THE PAPER: "Flying the same mission in 5 m/s of wind costs 26.9 s (+2.23 %) of makespan and turns a 0.20 % schedule prediction error into 2.43 %. Modelling that wind halves the prediction error (to 1.70 %, and from 7.08 % to 4.90 % on the worst aircraft) but does not shorten the mission — in this strip-parallel wind it lengthens it by 47.1 s, of which 44.0 s is a deliberately later release."

CAVEATS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THESE NUMBERS: one sortie per cell and SITL is deterministic, so there is no spread; `SIM_WIND_TURB = 0` and `SIM_WIND_T = 1` (constant wind at all altitudes), so gust, turbulence and shear are untested; 5 m/s is `Scenario.wind`'s default, not a site measurement; the 8 m/s case is a documented planner refusal (gust = 1.3 × wind exceeds the 8.0 m/s site limit at W ≥ 6.16 m/s), not a flight; and HV4W55S (5 m/s @180) could not be flown, so the cross-track half of the wind triangle is still unflown — the 270° evidence covers only the along-track half.
